Theorem
1. Theorem 1.24\group harmonic-functions Source: han-lin-lecture-notes:page-0018 ↗ hanlin:cor-green-normal-derivative For $\varphi \in C(\partial B_R)$, define \[ u(x)=\int _{\partial B_R}K(x,y)\varphi (y)\, d\sigma _y,\qquad |x|<R. \] Then $u$ is smooth and harmonic in $B_R$, continuous on $\overline{B_R}$, and $u=\varphi $ on $\partial B_R$.
Proof

\sketch Smoothness and harmonicity follow from the kernel properties. For boundary continuity, split the integral near and away from a boundary point; continuity of $\varphi $ controls the near part and uniform kernel decay controls the far part. The normalization $\int K=1$ completes the limit.

□
